newsitem.title: USA: Amgen stock drop linked to competitor.
newsitem.headline: Amgen stock drop linked to competitor.

text.p: Shares of biotech company Amgen Inc. fell sharply Monday in a drop some analysts linked to a competitive threat to its blockbuster Epogen drug.

They said the threat comes from Cambridge, Mass.-based Transkaryotic Therapies Inc., which is developing a product similar to Epogen, the Amgen drug widely used to treat renal failure in kidney dialysis patients.
Amgen fell $3.875 to $63 while Transkaryotic's stock rose $1.625 to $23.375 on Nasdaq.
Amgen in April sued Transkaryotic for patent infringement, but Transkaryotic maintains it has found a way to produce a drug that acts like Epogen without violating Amgen's patent.

Both companies declined to speculate on the reason for the stock moves but analysts said investors were responding to Transcaryotic's anouncement last week that it would begin trials of its drug shortly. Transcaryotic also said it had asked a federal court in Boston to dismiss Amgen's suit.
"A lot of people have been doing constant homework on this issue," said Pacific Growth Equities analyst Thomas Dietz. He said in his view Amgen's charge of patent infringement had no basis.

Any new drug shown to serve the same function as Epogen could pose a colossal threat to Amgen, the world's largest biotechnology company and one of the few so far that has been able to make a profit in the fledgling industry.

Epogen last year generated $1.1 billion in sales, more than half of Amgen's total revenues, and currently has no significant competition. Amgen has fought strenuously to protect and extend its Epogen patent, which currently runs through 2013 in the United States.

Despite the challenge it has posed, Transkaryotic still has a long legal battle ahead and the outcome is not at all certain. It is also not clear whether it will ultimately be successful in the lab in developing a drug that is as safe and effective as Epogen. Clinical trials are expected to take at least two years.
